title: Anne and Joachim
hook: tradition names Mary's parents; their feast is kept on 26 July

segments.voice: Yesterday, Peter and Cornelius, and the face-taker: a door opened to every nation. Your line was no one is unclean to god. A new week, and a whole week on one person: Mary.

Somebody taught you to tie your shoes. Somebody sat up with you through a fever. People like that are easy to forget, because they were simply always there. Mary had people like that: a mother and a father who carried her, fed her, and taught her to pray. Here's the honest part: the Bible never names them. Not once. The Gospels open with Mary already a young woman. The names Catholics use come from an early story told outside the Bible.
screen: `SOMEBODY TAUGHT YOU TO TIE YOUR SHOES.` → `MARY HAD PARENTS TOO.` → `THE BIBLE NEVER NAMES THEM.`

segments.voice: The story comes from an early Christian writing called the Protoevangelium of James. It's not in the Bible, and the Church has never treated it as Scripture, but its names and some of its scenes stuck. Here's how it tells it. Joachim is a good, generous man, but he and his wife Anne have no children, and at the temple he's shamed for it. So he goes out into the wilderness to fast and pray for forty days. At home, Anne sits in her garden and grieves. She looks up into a tree, sees a nest of baby birds, and weeps: even the birds have little ones. Then an angel comes to each of them, separately: you will have a child. Joachim hurries home, Anne runs to meet him at the city gate, and they embrace. Painters have come back to that moment again and again. Their daughter is Mary, and Anne, the story says, dedicates her to God. Anne is the English form of the Hebrew Hannah, meaning grace or favor, the name of the prophet Samuel's mother, who also prayed for a child for years. Catholics keep their feast together on July twenty-sixth, and as Jesus's grandparents, they're the patron saints of grandparents. Pope Francis even set aside a day in July for grandparents and older people, near their feast. Catholics read it as more than a sweet story: grace arriving through an ordinary family, slowly, through people who raised someone and are mostly forgotten.
screen: `AN OLD STORY, OUTSIDE THE BIBLE.` · `CHILDLESS, AND PRAYING.` · `THE EMBRACE AT THE GATE.` · `ANNE IS HANNAH: GRACE.` · then, large: `GRACE COMES THROUGH ORDINARY FAMILIES.`

segments.voice: Let a face come to mind, a parent, a grandparent, an aunt, a coach, a neighbor, anyone who helped raise you: not the perfect version, the real one. Remember one specific thing they did, a meal, a ride, a word, and let yourself be grateful for that one thing. If they've died, you can hold them with love; if you pray, you can thank God for them by name.
Hannah. The Hebrew name behind Anne, meaning grace, given to Mary's mother in an old, unbiblical story.
Your line: someone raised her too. Their names live on in an old story. Seventy-eight days and counting.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the memorial of Saints Joachim and Anne on 26 July, pray to them as patrons of grandparents, and many churches and shrines, like Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré in Quebec, are named for Anne.

trapdoor: what you thought: Mary's parents are in the Bible.
what it means: the Bible is silent; tradition names them Anne and Joachim and tells of a long-childless couple whose daughter was Mary.
what a scholar hears: the Protoevangelium of James, an early text never counted as Scripture, yet the source of their names and of the feast of Mary's presentation.

notes: Protoevangelium of James (c. 150): story summarized, not quoted; confirm the retelling (Joachim's offering rejected, 40 days in the wilderness, Anne and the sparrows' nest in a laurel tree, angels, embrace at the gate — the 'Golden Gate' in art).
Joachim and Anne share one memorial on 26 July since the 1969 calendar revision. Confirm.
World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly, instituted by Pope Francis in 2021, kept on the fourth Sunday of July. Confirm.
Name meanings: Hannah 'grace/favor'; Joachim (Yehoyakim) 'the Lord raises up / establishes'. Confirm.
Feast of the Presentation of Mary (21 November) derives from the same text; mentioned only in the trapdoor.
Outline hook uses '26 July'; American style in the voice says 'July twenty-sixth'.
